intro: Hi! You already know I want to go and I enjoy swimming. In this lesson you'll learn more verbs that take -ing (avoid, suggest, keep) or to (decide, afford, manage), and how to use -ing as the subject of a sentence and after words like in, at and before: Swimming is good for you, I'm interested in learning Japanese. Warm-up: what do you enjoy doing after work?
teachingNotes: Recap in one line only (taught in a2-verb-patterns): want, need, would like, hope, plan, decide, learn + to + base form; enjoy, finish, don't mind + -ing; to + base form for purpose. Build on it, don't re-teach it.

New verbs + -ing: avoid, suggest, consider, keep (= terus), mind (mostly don't mind / Do you mind ...?), practise (British spelling; American 'practice'), miss (= kangen melakukan), can't stand (= tidak tahan). New verbs + to: decide, plan, afford (almost always with can / can't / could), agree, refuse, promise, manage (= berhasil, not 'mengatur'), offer (= menawarkan diri), expect. There is no reliable meaning rule: present them as two lists to memorise, each verb learnt with its partner (avoid -ing, afford to).

Common errors: *'She suggested to go by train' (Indonesian 'menyarankan untuk pergi'; suggest takes -ing: suggested going), *'We can't afford buying a car' (afford takes to: can't afford to buy), *'I'm interested in learn English' (after a preposition always -ing: interested in learning), *'Swim is good for you' (Indonesian 'Berenang baik untuk kesehatan' doesn't change the verb; the subject needs -ing: Swimming is good for you, with a singular verb: is / takes).

-ing after prepositions: interested in, good at, tired of, afraid of, thanks for, before, after, without, instead of, how about. A preposition is followed by a noun or an -ing form, never the base form. before / after can also take a full clause (before I leave): accept both. 'look forward to + -ing' (to is a preposition there) may be mentioned as a phrase to remember, not tested.

Limits: never test like / love / hate / start / begin as either-or (both forms are correct). Mention stop / remember / try (meaning changes with -ing or to) only as a note, never test them. Don't teach verb + object + to (advise someone to), suggest + that clause (accept it if a learner writes it correctly), need + -ing, be / get used to + -ing, -ing participle clauses, passive infinitives, or perfect gerunds. Use A0–A2 grammar only: no past perfect, passive, reported speech, second conditional, relative clauses or used to.

keyPoints.title: Verb + -ing: avoid, suggest, consider, keep ...
keyPoints.explanation: After avoid, suggest, consider, keep, mind, practise, miss and can't stand, use verb + -ing, like after enjoy and finish. Indonesian 'menyarankan untuk pergi' makes people write 'suggested to go', but suggest takes -ing: She suggested going by train.

examples.en: I avoid driving in Jakarta at rush hour.
examples.id: Saya menghindari menyetir di Jakarta saat jam sibuk.

examples.en: Pak Hasan suggested meeting at the café near the office.
examples.id: Pak Hasan menyarankan bertemu di kafe dekat kantor.

id.title: Kata kerja + -ing: avoid, suggest, consider, keep ...
id.explanation: Setelah avoid, suggest, consider, keep, mind, practise, miss dan can't stand, pakai kata kerja + -ing, sama seperti setelah enjoy dan finish. Kata 'menyarankan untuk pergi' membuat banyak orang menulis 'suggested to go', padahal suggest memakai -ing: She suggested going by train.

keyPoints.title: Verb + to: decide, plan, afford, manage ...
keyPoints.explanation: After decide, plan, afford, agree, refuse, promise, manage, offer and expect, use to + base form, like after want and hope. afford usually comes with can / can't: We can't afford to buy a car, not 'can't afford buying'.

examples.en: Many young people can't afford to buy a house in Jakarta.
examples.id: Banyak anak muda tidak mampu membeli rumah di Jakarta.

examples.en: The traffic was terrible, but we managed to catch the train.
examples.id: Macetnya parah, tapi kami berhasil naik kereta itu.

examples.en: Dimas offered to drive me to the airport.
examples.id: Dimas menawarkan diri untuk mengantar saya ke bandara.

id.title: Kata kerja + to: decide, plan, afford, manage ...
id.explanation: Setelah decide, plan, afford, agree, refuse, promise, manage, offer dan expect, pakai to + bentuk dasar, sama seperti setelah want dan hope. afford biasanya dipakai dengan can / can't: We can't afford to buy a car, bukan 'can't afford buying'.

keyPoints.title: -ing as the subject and after prepositions
keyPoints.explanation: An -ing form can be the subject of a sentence, like a noun: Swimming is good for you (not 'Swim is good'), and the verb after it is singular (is, takes). After a preposition (in, at, of, for, before, after, without, instead of) use -ing too: I'm interested in learning English, not 'interested in learn'.

examples.en: Always check your ticket before leaving the station.
examples.id: Selalu cek tiketmu sebelum meninggalkan stasiun.

id.title: -ing sebagai subjek dan setelah preposisi
id.explanation: Bentuk -ing bisa menjadi subjek kalimat, seperti kata benda: Swimming is good for you (bukan 'Swim is good'), dan kata kerja setelahnya bentuk tunggal (is, takes). Setelah preposisi (in, at, of, for, before, after, without, instead of) pakai -ing juga: I'm interested in learning English, bukan 'interested in learn'.

acceptableAnswers: learning a new language takes time and patience

blocks.text: Quick recap: after **want, need, hope, plan, decide** you use **to + base form** (I want **to go**), and after **enjoy, finish, don't mind** you use the **-ing form** (I enjoy **swimming**). The **base form** is the plain verb from the dictionary (*go, buy*); the **-ing form** is the verb + -ing (*going, buying*). Now here are **eight more verbs + -ing**: **avoid, suggest, consider, keep, mind, practise, miss, can't stand**. As before, there's **no rule you can see**: learn each verb with its partner, like a new word (*avoid -ing*).

id.text: Ulang sebentar: setelah **want, need, hope, plan, decide** kamu memakai **to + bentuk dasar** (I want **to go**), dan setelah **enjoy, finish, don't mind** kamu memakai **bentuk -ing** (I enjoy **swimming**). **Bentuk dasar** adalah kata kerja polos seperti di kamus (*go, buy*); **bentuk -ing** adalah kata kerja + -ing (*going, buying*). Sekarang ini **delapan kata kerja lagi + -ing**: **avoid, suggest, consider, keep, mind, practise, miss, can't stand**. Seperti sebelumnya, **tidak ada aturan yang kelihatan**: hafalkan setiap kata kerja bersama pasangannya, seperti kosakata baru (*avoid -ing*).

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: *menyarankan **untuk** pergi*, *mempertimbangkan **untuk** pindah*. The word *untuk* makes many people write 'She suggested **to go**' or 'We're considering **to move**'. In English, **suggest** and **consider** take **-ing**: She suggested **going** by train. We're considering **moving**.

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *menyarankan **untuk** pergi*, *mempertimbangkan **untuk** pindah*. Kata *untuk* membuat banyak orang menulis 'She suggested **to go**' atau 'We're considering **to move**'. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **suggest** dan **consider** memakai **-ing**: She suggested **going** by train. We're considering **moving**.

blocks.text: **practise** is the British spelling of the verb; American English writes **practice** for the verb too. Both are correct, and both take -ing: I practise / practice **speaking** every day. **mind** is mostly used in questions and negatives: *Do you mind opening the window?* (Boleh tolong buka jendelanya?) — *I don't mind walking.*

id.text: **practise** adalah ejaan Inggris (British) untuk kata kerjanya; bahasa Inggris Amerika menulis **practice** juga untuk kata kerja. Keduanya benar, dan keduanya memakai -ing: I practise / practice **speaking** every day. **mind** kebanyakan dipakai dalam pertanyaan dan kalimat negatif: *Do you mind opening the window?* (Boleh tolong buka jendelanya?) — *I don't mind walking.*

blocks.prompt: It's cold in here. Do you mind ___ the door?
blocks.explain: mind is followed by verb + -ing: Do you mind closing the door? 'mind to close' and 'mind close' are wrong.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: It's cold in here. Do you mind ___ the door?
id.explain: mind diikuti kata kerja + -ing: Do you mind closing the door? 'mind to close' dan 'mind close' salah.

blocks.text: These verbs take **to + base form**, like *want* and *hope*: **decide, plan, afford, agree, refuse, promise, manage, offer, expect**. You already know *decide* and *plan*; the others are new. Many of them are about a choice or a result: you *decide*, *agree*, *refuse* or *promise* **to do** something, or you *manage* **to do** it.

id.text: Kata kerja ini memakai **to + bentuk dasar**, seperti *want* dan *hope*: **decide, plan, afford, agree, refuse, promise, manage, offer, expect**. *decide* dan *plan* sudah kamu kenal; yang lain baru. Banyak di antaranya tentang pilihan atau hasil: kamu *decide*, *agree*, *refuse* atau *promise* **to do** sesuatu, atau kamu *manage* **to do** sesuatu (berhasil melakukannya).

rows.en: Sari decided to look for a new job.
rows.id: Sari memutuskan untuk mencari pekerjaan baru.

rows.en: We're planning to open a small café in Bandung.
rows.id: Kami berencana membuka kafe kecil di Bandung.

rows.en: Many young people can't afford to buy a house in Jakarta.
rows.id: Banyak anak muda tidak mampu membeli rumah di Jakarta.

rows.en: My boss agreed to give me Friday off.
rows.id: Bos saya setuju memberi saya libur hari Jumat.

rows.en: The shop refused to give me a refund.
rows.id: Toko itu menolak mengembalikan uang saya.

rows.en: Rina promised to send the report tonight.
rows.id: Rina berjanji mengirim laporannya malam ini.

rows.en: The traffic was terrible, but we managed to catch the train.
rows.id: Macetnya parah, tapi kami berhasil naik kereta itu.

rows.en: Dimas offered to drive me to the airport.
rows.id: Dimas menawarkan diri untuk mengantar saya ke bandara.

rows.en: We expect to finish the project by Friday.
rows.id: Kami memperkirakan bisa menyelesaikan proyek ini paling lambat hari Jumat.

blocks.text: **afford** = mampu membayar (punya cukup uang atau waktu). It almost always comes with **can / can't / could**, and it takes **to**: We **can't afford to buy** a car. Not 'can't afford buying' and not 'can't afford buy'.

id.text: **afford** = mampu membayar (punya cukup uang atau waktu). Kata ini hampir selalu dipakai dengan **can / can't / could**, dan memakai **to**: We **can't afford to buy** a car. Bukan 'can't afford buying' dan bukan 'can't afford buy'.

blocks.text: Two meaning traps: **manage to** = *berhasil* (it was difficult, but you did it), not *mengatur*. (*manage a team* = mengelola tim is a different use, with a noun.) **offer to** = *menawarkan diri*: Dimas offered **to drive** me = Dimas offered to do it himself.

id.text: Dua jebakan arti: **manage to** = *berhasil* (sulit, tapi kamu bisa melakukannya), bukan *mengatur*. (*manage a team* = mengelola tim adalah pemakaian lain, dengan kata benda.) **offer to** = *menawarkan diri*: Dimas offered **to drive** me = Dimas sendiri yang menawarkan untuk mengantar.

blocks.prompt: Budi's laptop broke, but he managed ___ the report on time.
blocks.explain: manage (berhasil) is followed by to + base form: he managed to finish. manage never takes -ing.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Budi's laptop broke, but he managed ___ the report on time.
id.explain: manage (berhasil) diikuti to + bentuk dasar: he managed to finish. manage tidak pernah memakai -ing.

blocks.text: The **subject** is what a sentence is about, the word before the main verb (*Rina* works, *The train* is late). An activity can be the subject too, and then English uses the **-ing form**: **Swimming** is good for you. Here *swimming* works like a **noun** (a thing). Grammar books call this a **gerund**: just the -ing form used like a noun. The verb after it is **singular**, like after *it*: Swimming **is**, Cooking **takes** time.

id.text: **Subjek** adalah hal yang dibicarakan kalimat, kata sebelum kata kerja utama (*Rina* works, *The train* is late). Sebuah kegiatan juga bisa menjadi subjek, dan bahasa Inggris memakai **bentuk -ing**: **Swimming** is good for you. Di sini *swimming* berfungsi seperti **kata benda** (sebuah hal). Buku tata bahasa menyebutnya **gerund**: bentuk -ing yang dipakai seperti kata benda. Kata kerja setelahnya **tunggal**, seperti setelah *it*: Swimming **is**, Cooking **takes** time.

rows.en: Swimming is good for you.
rows.id: Berenang baik untuk kesehatanmu.

rows.en: Taking the KRL is cheaper than taking a taxi.
rows.id: Naik KRL lebih murah daripada naik taksi.

rows.en: Living in a big city can be stressful.
rows.id: Tinggal di kota besar bisa bikin stres.

rows.en: Reading the news every morning helps me at work.
rows.id: Membaca berita setiap pagi membantu saya di kantor.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: *Berenang baik untuk kesehatan* — the verb *berenang* doesn't change. So many learners write 'Swim is good for you'. In English, an activity at the start of a sentence needs **-ing**: **Swimming** is good for you. And the verb stays singular even when the -ing phrase is long: Reading the news every morning **helps** me (not *help*).

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Berenang baik untuk kesehatan* — kata kerja *berenang* tidak berubah. Jadi banyak orang menulis 'Swim is good for you'. Dalam bahasa Inggris, kegiatan di awal kalimat perlu **-ing**: **Swimming** is good for you. Dan kata kerjanya tetap tunggal walaupun frasa -ing-nya panjang: Reading the news every morning **helps** me (bukan *help*).

blocks.prompt: ___ in Jakarta traffic every day makes me tired.
blocks.explain: The activity is the subject of the sentence, so use the -ing form: Driving in Jakarta traffic ... 'Drive' is the base form, and 'to' never goes with -ing here.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ in Jakarta traffic every day makes me tired.
id.explain: Kegiatannya adalah subjek kalimat, jadi pakai bentuk -ing: Driving in Jakarta traffic ... 'Drive' adalah bentuk dasar, dan 'to' tidak dipakai bersama -ing di sini.

blocks.text: A **preposition** is a small word that links ideas, like *in, at, of, for, about, before, after, without, instead of* (= daripada / bukannya). After a preposition comes a **noun** (*interested in music*) or an **-ing form** (*interested in learning*), **never the base form**. So: I'm interested **in learning** English, not 'interested in learn'.

id.text: **Preposisi** (kata depan) adalah kata kecil yang menghubungkan ide, seperti *in, at, of, for, about, before, after, without, instead of* (= daripada / bukannya). Setelah preposisi datang **kata benda** (*interested in music*) atau **bentuk -ing** (*interested in learning*), **tidak pernah bentuk dasar**. Jadi: I'm interested **in learning** English, bukan 'interested in learn'.

rows.en: I'm interested in learning Japanese.
rows.id: Saya tertarik belajar bahasa Jepang.

rows.en: Rina is good at cooking.
rows.id: Rina pintar memasak.

rows.en: Always check your ticket before leaving the station.
rows.id: Selalu cek tiketmu sebelum meninggalkan stasiun.

rows.en: Why don't you take an ojek instead of walking?
rows.id: Kenapa kamu tidak naik ojek saja daripada jalan kaki?

rows.en: He left without saying goodbye.
rows.id: Dia pergi tanpa pamit.

rows.en: How about having lunch at the warung?
rows.id: Bagaimana kalau kita makan siang di warung?

blocks.text: **before / after** can take **-ing** (*before leaving*) or a full sentence with a subject (*before I leave*). Both are correct. What's wrong is the base form alone: not 'before leave'.

id.text: **before / after** bisa diikuti **-ing** (*before leaving*) atau kalimat lengkap dengan subjek (*before I leave*). Keduanya benar. Yang salah adalah bentuk dasar saja: bukan 'before leave'.

blocks.text: A phrase to remember from emails: **I look forward to meeting you** (Saya menantikan pertemuan dengan Anda). It looks strange — *to* + -ing? Here *to* is a **preposition** (like *to the bank*), not the *to* of *to go*. So -ing follows, as after any preposition. Learn it as a phrase.

id.text: Frasa yang perlu diingat dari email: **I look forward to meeting you** (Saya menantikan pertemuan dengan Anda). Kelihatannya aneh — *to* + -ing? Di sini *to* adalah **preposisi** (seperti *to the bank*), bukan *to* dari *to go*. Jadi setelahnya -ing, seperti setelah preposisi lain. Hafalkan sebagai satu frasa.

blocks.explain: for is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing: Thanks for sending me the link. 'for send' and 'for to send' are wrong.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Thanks for ___ me the link!
id.explain: for adalah preposisi, jadi kata kerja setelahnya memakai -ing: Thanks for sending me the link. 'for send' dan 'for to send' salah.

material.title: A note: verbs that take both

blocks.text: Some verbs take **both** forms. With **like, love, hate, start, begin** the meaning stays the same, so you never have to choose: *It started raining* = *It started to rain*. A few verbs, like **stop, remember** and **try**, **change their meaning** with -ing or to. You'll study them later; for now, just notice the difference with *stop*.

id.text: Beberapa kata kerja memakai **kedua** bentuk. Dengan **like, love, hate, start, begin** artinya tetap sama, jadi kamu tidak perlu memilih: *It started raining* = *It started to rain*. Beberapa kata kerja, seperti **stop, remember** dan **try**, **berubah artinya** dengan -ing atau to. Kamu akan mempelajarinya nanti; untuk sekarang, cukup perhatikan bedanya pada *stop*.

rows.en: It started raining. = It started to rain.
rows.id: Hujan mulai turun.

rows.en: My father stopped smoking last year.
rows.id: Ayah saya berhenti merokok tahun lalu.

rows.en: On the way home, we stopped to buy martabak.
rows.id: Dalam perjalanan pulang, kami berhenti untuk membeli martabak.
rows.note: stop + to = berhenti untuk (melakukan hal lain)

id.note: stop + to = berhenti untuk (melakukan hal lain)
